source_refs.note: Topic 20.4 (PDF 162); the book's 90% figure is attributed to it with a note.

blocks.text: A genetically modified organism (GMO) is a plant, animal or microbe whose genome has been changed. Transgenic organisms are a particular group of GMOs that have received DNA from a different, unrelated species.

The book states that about 90% of the canola, cotton, corn, soybean and sugar beet grown in the world is transgenic. Such high shares are reported for some countries, such as the United States; worldwide shares for several of these crops are lower.

blocks.explanation: No. A GMO is any organism with a changed genome; it is transgenic only if it has received DNA from a different, unrelated species.

items: GMO: genome changed; transgenic: carries DNA from another species.
